papers.title: Public acceptability, bioethics, and legal governance of wastewater and environmental surveillance for measles in South Africa
papers.abstract: Abstract Objectives This study investigates public opinion regarding the use of wastewater and environmental surveillance for measles in South African urban centres across ethical, legal, and public health policy themes, and maps these opinions onto existing bioethical and legal precedents. Design In-person field survey. Setting Three metropolitan catchment areas in Gauteng Province, South Africa (City of Tshwane, City of Ekurhuleni, and City of Johannesburg). Participants A sample of 100 adult community members residing or working within the selected sewer catchment areas. Primary outcome measures Baseline wastewater and environmental surveillance awareness, target-specific acceptability, spatial monitoring preferences, data-sharing comfort, and legal/privacy perceptions. Results Baseline awareness of WES was low (19%). Support was high for monitoring a range of biological and chemical targets using wastewater and environmental surveillance. However, acceptability was dependent on spatial scale: 83% supported macro-level "city-wide" monitoring, whereas support fell to 28% for localized sampling (individual homes and schools). Institutional trust in data handling was high among scientific and public health bodies. Conclusions Public acceptability of WES for communicable diseases, particularly measles, in urban South Africa is high but conditional upon macro-level data aggregation ("anonymity by aggregation") and governance by dedicated scientific entities. Given strong community support for measles surveillance and its alignment with the country’s bioethical and legal frameworks, the bioethical and legal requirements for this surveillance approach can be satisfied, paving the way for routine implementation of wastewater and environmental surveillance for communicable diseases.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 目的 本研究调查了南非城市中心关于废水使用和环境 麻疹 的公众意见,涵盖伦理、法律和公共卫生政策主题,并将这些意见映射到现有的生物伦理和法律先例。设计亲自实地调查。设置 南非豪登省的三个大都市集水区(茨瓦内市、艾库胡莱尼市和约翰内斯堡市)。参与者 在选定的下水道集水区居住或工作的 100 名成年社区成员作为样本。主要结果衡量基线废水和环境 监测 意识、特定目标的可接受性、空间监测偏好、数据共享舒适度以及法律/隐私认知。结果 WES 的基线认知度较低(19%)。使用废水和环境 监测 监测一系列生物和化学目标得到了高度支持。然而,可接受性取决于空间尺度:83%的人支持宏观层面的“全市范围”监测,而支持局部抽样(个人家庭和学校)的人则下降至28%。科学和公共卫生机构对数据处理的机构信任度很高。结论 在南非城市,公众对 WES 对传染病(特别是 麻疹)的接受度很高,但取决于宏观层面的数据聚合(“聚合匿名”)和专门科学实体的治理。鉴于社区对 麻疹 监测 的大力支持及其与国家生物伦理和法律框架的一致性,这种 麻疹 方法的生物伦理和法律要求可以得到满足,为针对传染病的废水和环境 监测 的常规实施铺平道路。

papers.title: Public health unit perspectives on challenges, barriers, and lessons learned from Ontario's 2024-2025 measles outbreak: a mixed-methods survey.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To systematically gather perspectives from public health units (PHUs) on the challenges, barriers, and lessons learned from the multi-jurisdictional measles outbreak in Ontario (October 2024-October 2025). METHODS: We conducted a mixed-methods survey in June/July 2025. We invited PHU staff involved with the measles outbreak and the Ministry of Health to respond to an online engagement survey. We analyzed multi-choice and ranked questions using counts and proportions. For open-ended questions, we conducted an inductive thematic analysis to identify common themes. RESULTS: We included 26 survey responses (83% response rate). At the time of the survey, about two-thirds (68%) of participating PHUs had at least one outbreak-associated case reported since October 2024. Respondents identified the lack of a comprehensive immunization registry (69%), immunization coverage below herd immunity thresholds (39%), workload demands or competing priorities (39%), and excluding susceptible contacts from school or work settings (39%) as their main challenges/barriers. For preparedness and response activities, respondents identified increased human resources capacity (63%) and use of technological tools (38%) for case and contact management as their most impactful strategies, along with enforcement or expansion of provincial school immunization legislation (42%). Lessons learned focused on timely and efficient outbreak response, supporting readiness, modernizing data systems and adopting technological innovations, standardizing and streamlining protocols, community engagement and relationship building, and strategic communications. CONCLUSION: Further public health efforts will be needed to continue to strengthen Ontario's immunization, surveillance, and outbreak preparedness and response actions. These will also contribute to Canada regaining its measles elimination status.

papers.abstract_zh: 目标:系统地收集公共卫生单位 (PHU) 对安大略省多司法管辖区 麻疹 暴发(2024 年 10 月至 2025 年 10 月)的挑战、障碍和经验教训的看法。方法:我们于 2025 年 6 月/7 月进行了一项混合方法调查。我们邀请参与 麻疹 暴发 和卫生部的 PHU 工作人员回答在线参与调查。我们分析了多项选择并使用计数和比例对问题进行了排名。对于开放式问题,我们进行了归纳主题分析,以确定共同主题。结果:我们纳入了 26 份调查回复(回复率为 83%)。截至调查时,大约三分之二 (68%) 的参与 PHU 自 2024 年 10 月以来报告了至少一例 暴发 相关病例。受访者认为,缺乏全面的免疫登记处 (69%)、免疫覆盖率低于群体免疫阈值 (39%)、工作量需求或竞争优先事项 (39%) 以及排除学校或工作环境中的易感接触者 (39%) 是他们的主要挑战/障碍。对于准备和应对活动,受访者认为增加人力资源能力(63%)和使用技术工具(38%)进行病例和接触者管理是最有影响力的策略,同时执行或扩大省级学校免疫立法(42%)。吸取的经验教训集中在及时有效的 暴发 响应、支持准备、现代化数据系统和采用技术创新、标准化和简化协议、社区参与和关系建设以及战略沟通。结论:需要进一步开展公共卫生工作,以继续加强安大略省的免疫接种、监测 和 暴发 的准备和应对行动。这些也将有助于加拿大重新获得 麻疹 消除地位。

papers.title: Communication and capacity in outbreak response: vaccination outreach to ultra-Orthodox communities during Israel's 2025 to 2026 measles outbreak: a mixed-methods study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Israel's largest measles outbreak since 2018-19 was traced to a single importation in April 2025, with transmission sustained in ultra-Orthodox Jewish communities; by April 2026, 3,624 cases and 17 deaths were recorded. Two explanations compete: community attitudes and messaging, or the physical availability of vaccination; this study examines both. Methods Mixed-methods retrospective study, January 2024 to August 2026, with the months to March 2025 as baseline. Six data streams were combined: epidemiological indicators; a census of Ministry of Health press releases on measles; 169 ultra-Orthodox media items coded by directed content analysis for frame, cited authority and topic, with inter-coder reliability assessed on a 20% sample; a dated series of documented changes in vaccination access; the government procurement register; and counter-vaccination material. Distributions were compared across periods by chi-square and Fisher exact tests. Results Both channels were quiet before the outbreak: 10 ministry releases and 10 community items in 2024. Pro-vaccination advocacy in community media rose from 8.3% of items pre-outbreak to 30.9% during escalation and fell to 17.6% in 2026 (p = 0.10). A rabbinic voice was cited in 14 items, all between May and December 2025 (Fisher p = 0.041), five of them chairs of medical-aid organisations rather than halachic authorities. No item amplified refusal. Access measures, including walk-in and extended-hours vaccination, were followed within two months by first-dose coverage gains among children aged 1 to 6 from 77% to 84% in Jerusalem and 72% to 82.6% in Beit Shemesh. Communication and vaccine access did not always move together: the peak month of official communication brought no documented access expansion, and the public vaccine station list was unchanged from August 2025 to January 2026. A contracted outreach array for the Ultra-Orthodox sector, tendered in 2020, ended in October 2023 and was not renewed; since then, outbreak outreach relied on small, tender-exempt engagements. Conclusions Ultra-Orthodox media were a receptive channel, and rabbinic and community engagement worked once activated. The principal constraint was capacity, not persuasion: standing outreach infrastructure, physical access and maintained public information. Sustaining these between outbreaks, and aligning communication with the access it promotes, are the priorities for measles control.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要背景 以色列自 2018-19 年以来最大的 麻疹 传播 可追溯到 2025 年 4 月的一次输入,传播 在极端正统犹太社区持续存在;截至 2026 年 4 月,已记录 3,624 例病例和 17 例死亡。有两种解释相互竞争:社区态度和消息传递,或者 疫苗接种 的实际可用性;这项研究对两者进行了检验。方法 混合方法回顾性研究,2024年1月至2026年8月,以截至2025年3月的月份为基线。合并了六个数据流:流行病学指标;卫生部关于 麻疹 的人口普查新闻稿;169 个极端正统媒体项目,通过针对框架、引用权威和主题的定向内容分析进行编码,并根据 20% 的样本评估编码器间的可靠性;疫苗接种 访问中一系列已记录的日期更改;政府采购登记册;和反疫苗接种材料。通过卡方检验和费舍尔精确检验比较不同时期的分布。结果 在 暴发 之前,两个渠道都很安静:2024 年有 10 个部委发布和 10 个社区项目。社区媒体中支持 疫苗接种 的宣传从 暴发 之前项目的 8.3% 上升到升级期间的 30.9%,并在 2026 年下降到 17.6%(p = 0.10)。2025 年 5 月至 12 月期间,有 14 个项目引用了拉比的声音(Fisher p = 0.041),其中 5 个项目是医疗援助组织的主席,而不是伊斯兰教权威。没有任何项目放大拒绝。在采取包括上门接种和延长 疫苗接种 服务时间在内的措施后,两个月内,1 至 6 岁儿童的第一剂接种覆盖率从耶路撒冷的 77% 提高到 84%,贝特谢梅什从 72% 提高到 82.6%。通信和 疫苗 访问并不总是一起进行:官方通信的高峰月没有带来有记录的访问扩展,并且公开的 疫苗 电台列表从 2025 年 8 月到 2026 年 1 月没有变化。超正统领域的合同外展阵列于 2020 年招标,于 2023 年 10 月结束,没有续签;从那时起,暴发 的外展活动就依赖于小型的、免招标的活动。结论 极端正统媒体是一个接受渠道,拉比和社区参与一旦激活就会发挥作用。主要的限制是能力,而不是说服力:固定的外展基础设施、物理访问和维护的公共信息。在 麻疹 之间维持这些,并将通信与其促进的访问保持一致,是 麻疹 控制的优先事项。

papers.title: Epidemiology of measles and its surveillance performance in the Oromia regional state of Ethiopia: Progress and challenges toward measles elimination goals
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Despite the effective vaccines and decades of experience towards elimination, measles remains a significant public health problem among children ≤ 15 years, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. A well-functioning surveillance system is essential for monitoring measles transmission and guiding control efforts. Towards this end we analyzed the epidemiology of measles and its surveillance system performance in the Oromia region, Ethiopia. Methods We analyzed the epidemiologic characteristics of the suspected-measles cases with laboratory results reported during 2006–2024 through the case-based surveillance. Frequencies, adjusted odds ratios (aORs), 95% confidence-intervals (CIs), and p-values were calculated using R statistical software. Surveillance performance was assessed using the non-measles febrile rash illness (NMFRI) and district-level surveillance indicators. Results A total of 25,674 suspected-measles cases with laboratory results were reported, of which 9,755 (38.3%) were measles IgM positive. Among confirmed cases, 5,173 (53.0%) were male and 78.2% occurred among children aged

papers.abstract: Background Delays in vaccination with the first/s dose of measles-containing vaccine (MCV1, MCV2) increases risk of measles transmission. MCV2 was added to Ethiopia's routine immunization schedule in 2019, administered at age 15 months. We describe age at measles vaccination and characteristics associated with timely vaccination following MCV2 introduction. Methods A secondary analysis from a 2021 cross-sectional household survey of children aged 12–35 months in Oromia, Ethiopia was conducted. MCV vaccination status and age at vaccination were determined from the child's vaccination card. The cumulative card-confirmed vaccination coverage of MCV1 and MCV2 (among children 24–35 months) by age at vaccination was estimated. Among children who received MCV, vaccination timing was classified as early (MCV1: <9 months; MCV2: <15 months), timely (MCV1: 9 to <10 months; MCV2: 15 to <16 months), or delayed (MCV1: ≥10 months; MCV2: ≥16 months). Characteristics associated with timely MCV1 vaccination were analyzed using multivariate logistic regression, with urban/rural stratification. Results Overall, 651 children aged 12–35 months (MCV1) and a subset of 270 children aged 24–35 months (MCV2) were analyzed. Cumulative MCV1 coverage was 59.9% by age 9 months and 76.3% by age 12 months, and MCV2 was 33.0% by age 15 months and 44.8% by age 24 months. MCV coverage was generally higher in urban compared to rural areas. Among vaccinated children, the proportion receiving early, timely, and delayed doses was 30.1%, 44.5%, and 25.3% for MCV1, and 28.6%, 41.2%, and 30.3% for MCV2, respectively. Characteristics associated with timely MCV1 vaccination differed in urban and rural areas, but common themes included increased caregiver immunization awareness and service delivery aspects. Conclusions Although most children who received MCV1 were vaccinated by 12 months, many received delayed doses. MCV2 coverage was low, irrespective of vaccination timing. Findings highlight the importance of routine catch-up vaccination policies and guidance, and the need for tailored strategies in urban and rural settings to improve MCV coverage and timely vaccination.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景 延迟 麻疹 与含 麻疹 的 疫苗(MCV1、MCV2)的首剂/次剂量会增加 麻疹 传播 的风险。MCV2 于 2019 年被添加到埃塞俄比亚的常规免疫计划中,在 15 个月大时接种。我们描述了 麻疹 疫苗接种 的年龄以及与 MCV2 引入后及时 疫苗接种 相关的特征。方法 对 2021 年埃塞俄比亚奥罗米亚州 12-35 个月龄儿童进行的横断面家庭调查进行了二次分析。MCV 疫苗接种 状态和 疫苗接种 年龄是根据孩子的 疫苗接种 卡确定的。估计了按 疫苗接种 年龄划分的 MCV1 和 MCV2(24-35 个月儿童)的累积卡确认 疫苗接种 覆盖率。在接受 MCV 的儿童中,疫苗接种 时间分为早期(MCV1:<9 个月;MCV2:<15 个月)、及时(MCV1:9 至 <10 个月;MCV2:15 至 <16 个月)或延迟(MCV1:≥10 个月;MCV2:≥16 个月)。使用多元逻辑回归和城市/农村分层分析与及时 MCV1 疫苗接种 相关的特征。结果 总体而言,对 651 名 12-35 个月的儿童 (MCV1) 和 270 名 24-35 个月的儿童 (MCV2) 进行了分析。9 个月时的累积 MCV1 覆盖率为 59.9%,12 个月时为 76.3%,15 个月时的 MCV2 累积覆盖率为 33.0%,24 个月时为 44.8%。与农村地区相比,城市地区的 MCV 覆盖率普遍较高。接种儿童中,MCV1 早期接种、及时接种和延迟接种比例分别为 30.1%、44.5% 和 25.3%,MCV2 接种比例分别为 28.6%、41.2% 和 30.3%。与及时 MCV1 疫苗接种 相关的特征在城市和农村地区有所不同,但共同主题包括护理人员免疫意识和服务提供方面的提高。结论 虽然大多数接受 MCV1 的儿童在 12 个月大时就接种了疫苗,但许多人接受了延迟剂量。无论 疫苗接种 时间如何,MCV2 覆盖率都很低。研究结果强调了常规追赶疫苗接种政策和指导的重要性,以及在城乡环境中制定量身定制的策略以提高MCV覆盖率和及时疫苗接种的必要性。

papers.title: Differences in Clinical Manifestations of Measles in Children with Complete and Incomplete Immunization History: Literature Review
papers.abstract: Measles is a highly contagious acute infectious disease. The six clinical manifestations assessed in this review are fever, cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, shortness of breath, and diarrhea. This literature review aims to analyze differences in these six manifestations in children based on their history or level of measles immunization completion. A search was conducted through PubMed, Google Scholar, and ScienceDirect, prioritizing original studies from 2020–2026. Articles in Indonesian, English, or other languages that were available in full text and could be adequately extracted were included. A total of five pediatric studies were included in the narrative and comparative synthesis. The results showed that fever was the most common symptom across all groups, thus limiting the ability to clinically differentiate immunization status. Cough, coryza, and diarrhea tended to be lower in vaccinated children in some studies, while findings regarding conjunctivitis were inconsistent. Direct evidence regarding shortness of breath is limited because most studies reported indirect respiratory indicators. In conclusion, a history of measles immunization tends to be associated with milder manifestations in some outcomes, but does not exclude the possibility of measles. Diagnosis still requires clinical assessment, epidemiological history, and laboratory confirmation.

papers.abstract_zh: 麻疹是一种传染性极强的急性传染病。本次评价评估的六种临床表现是发烧、咳嗽、鼻炎、结膜炎、气短和腹泻。本文献综述旨在根据儿童的麻疹免疫完成史或水平来分析儿童这六种表现的差异。通过 PubMed、Google Scholar 和 ScienceDirect 进行搜索,优先考虑 2020 年至 2026 年的原创研究。印度尼西亚语、英语或其他语言的文章均包含全文且可充分摘录。叙述和比较综合中总共纳入了五项儿科研究。结果表明,发烧是所有群体中最常见的症状,从而限制了临床区分免疫状态的能力。在一些研究中,接种疫苗的儿童的咳嗽、鼻炎和腹泻往往较少,而有关结膜炎的研究结果却不一致。关于呼吸短促的直接证据有限,因为大多数研究报告了间接呼吸指标。总之,麻疹 免疫史往往与某些结果中较轻的表现相关,但不排除 麻疹 的可能性。诊断仍需要临床评估、流行病学史和实验室确认。

papers.title: Waning Measles Immunity and Sustained Rubella Seroprotection Among Adults in Istanbul, Türkiye
papers.abstract: Background and Objectives: Despite long-standing MMR vaccination programmes, outbreaks of vaccine-preventable diseases continue to occur worldwide, raising concerns regarding waning immunity and susceptibility gaps in adult populations. Between 2017 and 2019 alone, WHO reported over 880,000 measles cases globally—a fourfold increase over the preceding two years—with outbreaks in both low- and high-income countries despite high childhood vaccination coverage. This study evaluated the seroepidemiology of measles, mumps, and rubella among adults in Türkiye over a nine-year period. Materials and Methods: A retrospective laboratory-based study was conducted using ELISA IgM and IgG results obtained between 2014 and 2022 at a tertiary-care university hospital. Seropositivity rates were analysed by year, age group, and sex. Temporal trends were assessed using the Cochran–Armitage trend test; factors associated with IgG seropositivity were assessed using multivariable logistic regression. Results: Among 10,407 adult test records, overall IgG seropositivity was 75.8% for measles, 94.9% for rubella, and 86.3% for mumps; IgM positivity remained low throughout (0.9%, 0.4%, and 1.9%, respectively). Measles IgG declined significantly from 78.4% in 2014–2019 to 62.6% in 2022 (p < 0.001), whereas Rubella IgG remained stable (93.2–95.7%) and Mumps IgG showed no significant temporal change. Seropositivity increased markedly with age for measles (18–29 years: 70.2% vs. ≥50 years: 93.4%; p < 0.001) and mumps (p = 0.030). Multivariable analysis confirmed that Measles IgG seropositivity was substantially lower in 2022 than in the pooled 2014–2019 period (OR = 0.432, 95% CI: 0.319–0.584, p < 0.001). Rubella seroprotection among women of reproductive age was 94.7% (95% CI: 93.9–95.5%), close to but not statistically distinguishable from the 95% population immunity benchmark used in rubella elimination frameworks. Conclusions: A significant measles immunity gap exists among younger adults in Türkiye, with Measles IgG seropositivity declining from 78.4% in 2014–2019 to 62.6% in 2022, consistent with a cohort effect whereby vaccine-era cohorts exhibit lower protection than older adults with naturally acquired immunity. Rubella immunity, by contrast, remained close to the 95% elimination benchmark throughout. These findings underscore the importance of targeted serological surveillance and evidence-based booster vaccination strategies.

papers.title: Antiviral Therapy for Measles: Progress, Challenges and Perspectives
papers.abstract: Introduction/Objective Despite the availability of an effective vaccine, measles remains a major cause of pediatric morbidity and mortality worldwide. This review aims to evaluate advances toward the development of specific antiviral treatments for measles by examining current candidates, their molecular targets, available preclinical and clinical data, and key challenges to therapeutic application. Methods An extensive literature search (2000-2026) was conducted using PubMed and official databases (WHO, CDC), including in vitro and in vivo studies (animal models), clinical trials, and international guidelines. The main agents included were ribavirin, favipiravir, remdesivir, ERDRP-0519, GHP-88309, fusion peptide inhibitors, and monoclonal antibodies. Results No antiviral is yet approved specifically for measles; however, several candidates show promise. Ribavirin, a broad-spectrum antiviral, has demonstrated in vitro inhibition of measles virus and clinical benefit in severe cases (especially in immunocompromised patients), although data remain limited. Novel polymerase inhibitors such as ERDRP-0519 and its derivative GHP-88309 have shown effective post-exposure protection in animal models. Nucleoside analogs initially developed for other viruses (favipiravir, remdesivir) exhibit in vitro anti-measles activity. Peptides and monoclonal antibodies targeting the viral fusion protein also demonstrate encouraging results. Discussion Antiviral therapy may improve the management of severe or post-exposure cases, especially in non-vaccinable individuals. Conclusion While vaccination remains the cornerstone of prevention, antiviral therapy may improve the management of severe or post-exposure cases, especially in non-vaccinable individuals. Clinical trials are needed to validate these strategies and consider their integration into future global measles elimination programs.

papers.title_zh: Antiviral Therapy for Measles: Progress, Challenges and Perspectives
papers.source_body_en: Introduction/Objective Despite the availability of an effective vaccine, measles remains a major cause of pediatric morbidity and mortality worldwide. This review aims to evaluate advances toward the development of specific antiviral treatments for measles by examining current candidates, their molecular targets, available preclinical and clinical data, and key challenges to therapeutic application. Methods An extensive literature search (2000-2026) was conducted using PubMed and official databases (WHO, CDC), including in vitro and in vivo studies (animal models), clinical trials, and international guidelines. The main agents included were ribavirin, favipiravir, remdesivir, ERDRP-0519, GHP-88309, fusion peptide inhibitors, and monoclonal antibodies. Results No antiviral is yet approved specifically for measles; however, several candidates show promise. Ribavirin, a broad-spectrum antiviral, has demonstrated in vitro inhibition of measles virus and clinical benefit in severe cases (especially in immunocompromised patients), although data remain limited. Novel polymerase inhibitors such as ERDRP-0519 and its derivative GHP-88309 have shown effective post-exposure protection in animal models. Nucleoside analogs initially developed for other viruses (favipiravir, remdesivir) exhibit in vitro anti-measles activity. Peptides and monoclonal antibodies targeting the viral fusion protein also demonstrate encouraging results. Discussion Antiviral therapy may improve the management of severe or post-exposure cases, especially in non-vaccinable individuals. Conclusion While vaccination remains the cornerstone of prevention, antiviral therapy may improve the management of severe or post-exposure cases, especially in non-vaccinable individuals. Clinical trials are needed to validate these strategies and consider their integration into future global measles elimination programs.

papers.title: Measles immunity in a large urban population in Northeast Brazil: a population-based assessment using PRNT and ELISA.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Waning measles immunity in post-elimination settings may increase susceptibility and facilitate viral reintroduction. This study assessed measles immunity in an urban population in Northeast Brazil using neutralizing antibody testing and IgG serology. METHODS: A population-based seroprevalence study was conducted in 2024 among residents aged ≥2 years in 30 sentinel areas of Salvador, Brazil. Measles-specific IgG antibodies were measured by ELISA in all participants, and neutralizing antibodies were assessed by plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT) in a stratified subsample (n=671). Seroprevalence was estimated by age group. Agreement between ELISA and PRNT was evaluated using Cohen's kappa, and factors associated with PRNT positivity were examined using logistic regression adjusted for age and sex. RESULTS: Among participants, 60.8% were female and 38.3% were aged ≥50 years. Overall seroprevalence was 91.4% by PRNT and 85.4% by ELISA, with 86.3% agreement between assays (kappa = 0.34, p < 0.001). The highest PRNT seropositivity was observed among individuals aged 10-19 years and ≥50 years, whereas the highest PRNT seronegativity occurred among young adults aged 20-29 years (23.4%). In adjusted analyses, children and adolescents aged 5-19 years had lower odds of PRNT positivity compared with those aged 2-4 years. No significant differences were observed by sex. CONCLUSIONS: Despite high overall seroprevalence, relevant immunity gaps were identified, particularly among young adults, indicating increased susceptibility to measles in this urban population. The combined use of PRNT and ELISA highlights the need for targeted vaccination strategies in post-elimination urban settings.

papers.abstract_zh: 目的:消除后环境中 麻疹 免疫力的减弱可能会增加易感性并促进病毒重新引入。本研究使用中和抗体测试和 IgG 血清学 评估了巴西东北部城市人口的 麻疹 免疫力。方法:2024 年,在巴西萨尔瓦多 30 个哨点地区的 2 岁以上居民中开展了一项基于人群的 血清流行率 研究。通过 ELISA 测量所有参与者的 麻疹 特异性 IgG 抗体,并通过分层子样本 (n=671) 中的空斑减少中和试验 (PRNT) 评估中和抗体。血清流行率 按年龄组估计。使用 Cohen's kappa 评估 ELISA 和 PRNT 之间的一致性,并使用调整年龄和性别的逻辑回归检查与 PRNT 阳性相关的因素。结果:参与者中,60.8%为女性,38.3%年龄≥50岁。PRNT 的总体 血清流行率 为 91.4%,ELISA 的总体 血清流行率 为 85.4%,测定之间的一致性为 86.3%(kappa = 0.34,p < 0.001)。PRNT 血清阳性率最高的人群为 10-19 岁和 50 岁以上人群,而最高的 PRNT 血清阴性人群为 20-29 岁的年轻人 (23.4%)。在调整后的分析中,5-19 岁的儿童和青少年 PRNT 阳性的几率低于 2-4 岁的儿童和青少年。没有观察到性别之间的显着差异。结论:尽管 血清流行率 总体较高,但仍发现了相关的免疫差距,特别是在年轻人中,表明该城市人群对 麻疹 的易感性增加。PRNT 和 ELISA 的结合使用凸显了在消除后城市环境中采取有针对性的 疫苗接种 策略的必要性。

papers.title: Five-year descriptive epidemiology of measles in Punjab, Pakistan, 2022–2026: trends, age distribution, and geographic burden; a retrospective surveillance study
papers.abstract: Measles resurgences following the COVID-19 pandemic have placed millions of unvaccinated children at risk across South Asia. Punjab, Pakistan’s most populous province with approximately 125 million residents, experienced a sustained measles epidemic from 2022 to 2024. This study describes the five-year epidemiology of measles in Punjab using individual-level surveillance data from the provincial Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI) surveillance system. We conducted a retrospective descriptive analysis of 72,565 suspected measles case records from the Punjab EPI VPD surveillance line-list, epidemiological week 1 of 2022 through epidemiological week 23 of 2026. Variables analyzed included case counts, incidence rates per 100,000 population, age at illness onset, sex, vaccination status, case outcomes, and district-level geographic distribution. District-level population denominators adjusted for annual growth were applied to calculate incidence rates. Statistical analysis used the Cochran-Armitage trend test, Wilson 95% confidence intervals, and Spearman rank correlation. Reported measles cases escalated from 6,613 in 2022 to a peak of 23,623 in 2024 (incidence 18.92 per 100,000 population), before declining to 19,913 in 2025 and 9,898 through week 23 of 2026. Overall, 184 deaths were recorded (case fatality ratio [CFR] 0.25%). Male cases predominated (57–58% annually; M:F ratio 1.40:1). The proportion of infants under 12 months rose from 37.3% (95% CI 36.2–38.5%) in 2022 to 47.9% (95% CI 46.9–48.9%) in 2026 (Cochran-Armitage z = 12.77, p < 0.0001), with median age at infection declining from 18 months (IQR 8–42) to 12 months (IQR 7–36). Zero-dose cases peaked at 49.6% (95% CI 49.0–50.2%) in 2024 (z = 3.37, p = 0.0008). Chiniot (62.95 per 100,000) and Jhang (59.98 per 100,000) bore the highest district incidence in 2024. Reported first-dose measles-containing vaccine (MCV1) coverage was paradoxically positively correlated with district measles incidence (Spearman rho = + 0.370, p = 0.027), consistent with surveillance activity bias. Punjab experienced a measles epidemic peaking in 2024, with 72,565 reported suspected cases and 184 deaths across 2022 to 2026, driven by accumulation of unvaccinated children within districts reporting nominally high MCV1 coverage. The progressive shift in disease burden toward infants under 12 months demands renewed focus on vaccination system quality, zero-dose outreach, and surveillance sensitivity. These findings are relevant to other high-burden EMRO settings facing similar immunization system challenges.

papers.full_text: Coroner confirms US measles death while CDC count remains at zero amid row over the fatalities BMJ 2026; 394 doi: https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj-2026-100789 (Published 08 September 2026) Cite this as: BMJ 2026;394:e100789 A child has been confirmed to have died of measles by the coroner of Lancaster County, Pennsylvania—the first such death in Pennsylvania for 35 years.1 It follows intense scrutiny over the case, in which US health officials sought to downplay reports that two recent infant deaths in the county were caused by the disease. Stephen Diamantoni, Lancaster County coroner, told The BMJ that the death of a six week old girl on 18 August was “caused by measles.” The girl also had Amish lethal microcephaly. “The average life expectancy with this condition is 4 to 6 months of age. Because of the compromised state of these children many die of respiratory infections,” Diamantoni said. He first confirmed to US media at the weekend that measles had caused the girl’s death.2 US health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, who previously referred to “so called measles deaths”3 in Lancaster County, acknowledged and appeared to accept the update on social media.4 As of Tuesday morning, however the US Centers for Disease Control & Prevention (CDC) still had not updated its web page on US measles statistics to include the death.5 A statement on that page simply says that there are currently no death records that indicate measles as the “underlying cause.” It adds that the CDC is developing a new “standardised case definition for deaths due to measles.” The agency does say that there have been 3134 measles cases in the US to date this year, already significantly higher than last year’s total of 2289. The BMJ approached the CDC for comment. The Lancaster County coroner’s update is the latest development in a very public saga around two child deaths in his jurisdiction described as “measles associated” by the Pennsylvania Department of Health in a statement on 25 August.6 On 26 August, Kennedy Jr claimed in a social media post that “the deaths may even have been altogether fabricated” and cited information from the county coroner, which, at the time, did not show any record of measles deaths.7 “I have thoroughly reviewed the case investigation information and sadly can confirm that there were two recent measles associated deaths in Lancaster County,” said Pennsylvania health secretary Debra Bogen in a response on social media posted on 27 August.8 Diamantoni has similarly referred to two child deaths in Lancaster County, the six week old Amish girl and a newborn baby boy who had a ruptured spleen. “Our forensic pathologist . . . felt that this was traumatic and not related to measles, as the spleen was not enlarged or inflamed,” he told The BMJ. “We are continuing our investigation as to what may have caused the laceration.” While Diamantoni suggested the case of the newborn boy was one of the “measles associated” deaths cited by the Pennsylvania Department of Health, he added, “I am uncertain whether the death of the 6 week infant is the [second] death that they referred to.” The BMJ has approached the Pennsylvania Department of Health for clarification. Arguments have erupted on social media over whether the children’s deaths were “measles associated” or “measles caused.” But David Elliman, a community paediatrician and honorary associate professor at University College London, said this is merely “playing with words.” “You wonder how much of this is based on medicine and how much it is based on politics,” he told The BMJ, arguing that the Lancaster County situation was leading to “continued confusion and destruction of trust in what were established bodies.” Elliman pointed out that, because babies are too young to be immunised against measles, the only means of protecting them from this highly contagious disease was through vaccinating older people to establish herd immunity. Vaccination rates for measles are currently falling in the US.9 Ian Jones, professor of virology at the University of Reading, said unfounded scepticism around the measles vaccine was a cause for concern. “It’s a smouldering situation that is just not getting any better-and that will lead, ultimately, to further deaths,” he said. “Not at a huge rate, but where measles is a significant factor in the outcome.”

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 目前,美国 麻疹 的 疫苗接种 比率正在下降。9 雷丁大学病毒学教授伊恩·琼斯 (Ian Jones) 表示,对 麻疹 疫苗 毫无根据的怀疑令人担忧。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 他在周末首次向美国媒体证实,麻疹 导致了女孩的死亡。2 此前提到兰卡斯特县“所谓的 麻疹 死亡”3 的美国卫生部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪 (Robert F Kennedy Jr) 在社交媒体上承认并似乎接受了这一更新。4 截至周二上午,美国疾病控制与预防中心 (CDC) 仍未更新其有关美国 麻疹 统计数据的网页,将死亡纳入其中。5该页面上的一份声明只是说,目前没有死亡记录表明 麻疹 是“根本原因”。它还补充说,疾病预防控制中心正在制定新的“因 麻疹 死亡的标准化病例定义”。该机构确实表示,今年迄今为止,美国已有 3134 起 麻疹 案件,已明显高于去年的 2289 起案件总数。
elements_zh.methods: 所提供的证据没有明确说明核心实验、分析或统计方法。
elements_zh.main_results: Coroner confirms US measles death while CDC count remains at zero amid row over the fatalities BMJ 2026; 394 doi: https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj-2026-100789 (Published 08 September 2026) Cite this as: BMJ 2026;394:e100789 A child has been confirmed to have died of measles by the coroner of Lancaster County, Pennsylvania—the first such death in Pennsylvania for 35 years.1 It follows intense scrutiny over the case, in which US health officials sought to downplay reports that two recent infant deaths in the county were caused by the disease.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 社交媒体上爆发了关于孩子们的死亡是“麻疹相关”还是“麻疹造成”的争论。但伦敦大学学院名誉副教授、社区儿科医生大卫·埃利曼表示,这只是“文字游戏”。他告诉《英国医学杂志》:“你想知道其中有多少是基于医学,有多少是基于政治。”他认为兰开斯特县的情况导致“对现有机构的信任持续混乱和破坏”。埃利曼指出,由于婴儿太小,无法接种麻疹疫苗,因此保护他们免受这种高度传染性疾病的唯一方法是通过给老年人接种疫苗来建立群体免疫力。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 他说:“情况一直在恶化,而且没有任何好转,最终将导致更多人死亡。”
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: “我们正在继续调查可能导致撕裂的原因。”虽然迪亚曼托尼表示,这名新生男婴的病例是宾夕法尼亚州卫生部引用的“麻疹 相关”死亡事件之一,但他补充说,“我不确定这名 6 周婴儿的死亡是否是他们提到的第二起死亡事件。”英国医学杂志已联系宾夕法尼亚州卫生部寻求澄清。

papers.title: EPIDEMIOLOGICAL PROFILE OF MEASLES HOSPITALIZATIONS IN BRAZIL FROM 2020 TO 2025
papers.abstract: Objective: To analyze the epidemiological profile of hospital admissions due to measles in Brazil from 2020 to 2025. Methods: This was an ecological, descriptive, retrospective study based on secondary data from the Hospital Information System of the Brazilian Unified Health System (SIH/SUS), available through DATASUS/TABNET. Hospital admissions, deaths, and mortality rates were analyzed according to year, geographic region, sex, race/ethnicity, and age group, considering measles as the primary diagnosis (ICD-10 B05). Results: A total of 940 hospital admissions and eight deaths were recorded during the study period. A marked reduction in hospital admissions was observed between 2020 and 2023, followed by a slight increase in 2024 and 2025. The North region accounted for the highest proportion of hospitalizations (58.62%), while children under 1 year of age had the highest number of admissions, followed by those aged 1 to 4 years. The highest proportional mortality was observed among individuals aged 80 years or older. Hospitalizations were similarly distributed between sexes, with a predominance of the brown race/ethnicity category among records with available information. Conclusion: Measles-related hospital admissions decreased substantially during the study period; however, the persistence of hospitalizations and the increase observed in recent years highlight the need to maintain high vaccination coverage, continuous epidemiological surveillance, timely diagnosis, and ongoing training of healthcare professionals to prevent viral reintroduction and sustained transmission in Brazil.

papers.abstract_zh: 目的:分析 2020 年至 2025 年巴西因 麻疹 住院的流行病学概况。方法:这是一项生态、描述性、回顾性研究,基于巴西统一卫生系统 (SIH/SUS) 医院信息系统(可通过 DATASUS/TABNET 获取)的二手数据。根据年份、地理区域、性别、种族/民族和年龄组对入院率、死亡率和 死亡率 率进行分析,并将 麻疹 视为主要 死亡率 (ICD-10 B05)。结果:研究期间共有 940 人入院,8 人死亡。2020年至2023年住院人数明显减少,随后2024年至2025年略有增加。北部地区住院人数比例最高(58.62%),其中1岁以下儿童住院人数最多,其次是1至4岁儿童。在 80 岁或以上的个体中观察到 死亡率 比例最高。住院治疗在性别之间的分布也类似,在现有信息的记录中,棕色人种/族裔类别占主导地位。结论:研究期间,麻疹 相关住院人数大幅减少;然而,住院治疗的持续存在和近年来观察到的增加凸显了巴西需要保持高 疫苗接种 覆盖率、持续的流行病学 监测、及时的 诊断 以及对医疗保健专业人员的持续培训,以防止巴西病毒重新引入和持续的 传播。

papers.title: SVIR Model Analysis of Measles with Incomplete Vaccination and 1 Waning Immunity: Sidoarjo-Indonesia Case
papers.abstract: Measles remains a significant public health challenge in Indonesia, especially in regionswith heterogeneous vaccination coverage and waning immunity. This study develops andanalyzes a Susceptible–Vaccinated–Infected–Recovered (SVIR) compartmental model formeasles transmission in Sidoarjo City, Indonesia, incorporating waning immunity. The basicreproduction number R0 is derived using the next-generation matrix method, and the globalstability of both the disease-free and endemic equilibria is rigorously proven via Lyapunovfunctions. Model parameters are estimated from weekly 2023 surveillance data in Sidoarjo Cityusing Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Extended Kalman Filter, Maximum LikelihoodEstimation, and Least Squares, and evaluated via Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE).PSO achieves the lowest MAPE (11.17%), outperforming the other methods. The estimatedR0 = 0.668confirms a disease-free regime. Normalized sensitivity analysis identifies vaccineefficacy as the most influential parameter; a decline in efficacy to0 .75elevates R0 close tothe critical threshold, and any further reduction pushes the system into an endemic state.These findings underscore the necessity of maintaining high vaccine efficacy through boosterprograms and strengthened immunization strategies to sustain measles elimination at thedistrict level.

This study develops andanalyzes a Susceptible–Vaccinated–Infected–Recovered (SVIR) compartmental model formeasles transmission in Sidoarjo City, Indonesia, incorporating waning immunity. The basicreproduction number R0 is derived using the next-generation matrix method, and the globalstability of both the disease-free and endemic equilibria is rigorously proven via Lyapunovfunctions. Model parameters are estimated from weekly 2023 surveillance data in Sidoarjo Cityusing Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Extended Kalman Filter, Maximum LikelihoodEstimation, and Least Squares, and evaluated via Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE).PSO achieves the lowest MAPE (11.17%), outperforming the other methods. The estimatedR0 = 0.668confirms a disease-free regime. Normalized sensitivity analysis identifies vaccineefficacy as the most influential parameter; a decline in efficacy to0 .75elevates R0 close tothe critical threshold, and any further reduction pushes the system into an endemic state.These findings underscore the necessity of maintaining high vaccine efficacy through boosterprograms and strengthened immunization strategies to sustain measles elimination at thedistrict level.
source_records.journal: CAUCHY: Jurnal Matematika Murni dan Aplikasi

papers.title: Fuzzy based Mathematical Model of Measles with Double-Dose Vaccination under Epidemiological Parameter Uncertainty
papers.abstract: This study develops a fuzzy-based mathematical model for the transmission dynamics of measles incorporating double-dose vaccination and treatment under epidemiological parameter uncertainty. The model extends a deterministic measles framework by representing selected parameters, including the transmission, vaccination, treatment and recovery rates, as triangular fuzzy numbers. Basic properties of the model are established, and the disease-free equilibrium and basic reproduction number are derived. The $r$-cut approach is employed to obtain interval-valued representations of the uncertain parameters and the fuzzy basic reproduction number. The results show that the uncertainty interval of the reproduction number decreases as the $r$-cut level increases and converges to the deterministic reproduction number at $r=1$. Intervention analysis further shows that a combined reduction in disease transmission with increased vaccination coverage and treatment can reduce both the deterministic reproduction number and the upper bound of the fuzzy reproduction number below unity. The proposed framework therefore provides a useful approach for assessing measles transmission and control when epidemiological parameters are imprecisely known.

papers.title: Measles, Mumps, and Rubella - Persistence of Immunity After Childhood Vaccination in Australian Health Science Students
papers.abstract: Measles, Mumps, and Rubella (MMR) continue to pose global public health risks, and immunity among undergraduate health science students is essential to ensure safe clinical placement and workforce readiness. Despite high childhood vaccination coverage, emerging evidence suggests that some young adults may have incomplete, waning, or uncertain immunity. This program of research aimed to evaluate the long-term effectiveness of the MMR vaccine from childhood through to adulthood among undergraduate health science students. Three studies explored biological, behavioural, and system-level contributors to immunity gaps. Paper 1 used a scoping review methodology to map how the nurse practitioner (NP) immuniser role is conceptualised within primary healthcare (PHC). The review found that although NPs frequently deliver vaccination-related care, their role in immunisation assessment and follow-up is under-recognised, revealing opportunities for NPled models to address barriers and improve vaccine communication. Paper 2 used a quantitative cohort study, using the Vaccine Effectiveness Framework, to compare Australian Immunisation Register (AIR) records with serological testing among domestic and international students. Discrepancies were identified between documented vaccination and actual immune status, including students with complete AIR records who lacked serological immunity, providing evidence of waning immunity and limitations of relying solely on administrative records. Paper 3 used a quantitative cross-sectional survey informed by the Health Belief Model (HBM) to examine students’ knowledge, attitudes, and beliefs about MMR diseases, vaccination, and immunity testing. Knowledge gaps, low perceived susceptibility, misconceptions about lifelong immunity, and difficulty interpreting vaccination records were strongly associated with reduced intention to check immunity, highlighting the need for structured education within health science programs. Together, these studies demonstrate that immunity gaps arise from the intersection of biological waning immunity, incomplete or unreliable records, and behavioural influences on vaccine decisionmaking. This program of research fills a critical gap by integrating biological, behavioural, and system level evidence and demonstrates the potential for NP-led immunisation models to strengthen assessment, communication, and follow-up in primary healthcare. The findings offer practical strategies to improve vaccine literacy, immunity monitoring, and long-term immunity among future healthcare professionals.

papers.title: The 2026 Measles Outbreak in Bangladesh: A Critique of Immunity Gaps and Care Deficiencies
papers.abstract: Bangladesh entered 2026 amid a severe measles outbreak that peaked in mid-May. This article analyses the public health response to the outbreak and evaluates the government's management of the crisis. Health professionals and measles experts have attributed the outbreak to accumulated gaps in routine immunisation, weaknesses in public health infrastructure, poor nutritional status among children, widespread vitamin A deficiency, and maternal undernutrition during pregnancy and breastfeeding.

papers.full_text: SPECIAL CLINICAL REVIEW PEER-REVIEWED Measles: A resurgent threat and the role of pharmacists in prevention Fawziah Marra BSc(Pharm), PharmD, FCSHP, ACPR, RPh1, Roxane Carr BSc(Pharm), PharmD, FCSHP, ACPR, RPh1,2 Overview Considered eliminated in Canada over 25 years ago, measles has re-emerged as a public health concern due to declining vaccination rates and increased global travel. In fact, recently Canada, and by extension all the Americas, has been stripped of its measles-free certification by the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) after failing to curb an outbreak of the virus for 12 consecutive months.1 The majority of the outbreak cases stem from undervaccinated communities in Alberta and Ontario, although cases have been reported in most provinces and territories. To regain its measles elimination status, vac- cination of the population will play a vital role. As accessible health care providers, pharmacists are in a unique position to detect early signs of disease, educate the public, and play a vital role in vaccination programs. Epidemiology The measles virus is a member of the Paramyxoviridae family, which includes mumps, parainfluenza, and respiratory syncy- tial (RSV) viruses.2 Infection with measles results in lifelong immunity.2 Measles is a nationally notifiable disease.3 The live- attenuated vaccine, containing measles only, was introduced into Canadian routine immunization programs in the early 1970s.4 Between 1974 and 1983, a 1-dose combined vaccine for measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) was introduced. How- ever, Canada moved to the 2-dose MMR vaccine series between 1996 and 1997 with school-based catch-up to ensure chil- 1Faculty of Pharmaceutical Sciences, University of British Columbia, Vancouver, BC; 2BC Children’s Hospital, Vancouver, BC Correspondence: Fawziah Marra, (fawziah@mail.ubc.ca). dren had 2 doses.3,4 Between 1970 and 2024, measles cases decreased by more than 99%.4 The success of the 2-dose MMR campaign allowed Canada to achieve measles elimination status in 1998.3 However, spo- radic outbreaks continued to occur, primarily due to the importation of cases from regions of the world with ongoing transmission or transmission from clusters of unvaccinated individuals. From 1998 to 2023, an average of 91 measles cases were reported annually, ranging between 0 and 752 cases (Figure 1).4 Unfortunately, the number of cases in 2025 has increased exponentially.5 As of November 8, 2025, a total of 5208 measles cases were reported by 10 jurisdictions (Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, New Brunswick, Northwest Territories, Nova Scotia, Ontario, Prince Edward Island, Quebec, and Saskatchewan) (Figure 2).6 Most cases occur in children under 5 and adolescents, particularly those unvaccinated or undervaccinated. Transmission Humans are the only reservoir for measles. The basic repro- duction number (R0) is estimated to be between 12 and 18 (i.e., one infected person will go on to infect 12 to 18 other people). This is approximately 10 times higher than for COVID-19 or influenza,7 making measles one of the most infectious known pathogens. The virus primarily spreads through airborne res- piratory droplets and aerosolized droplet nuclei, which can remain infectious in the air or on surfaces for up to 2 hours © Canadian Pharmacists Association (CPhA), 2026. Please visit https://utppublishing.com/ resources/rights-and-permissions/journals for details. 32 C P J / R P C r J A N U A RY / F E B R U A RY 2 0 2 6 r V O L 1 5 9 , N O 1 DOI:10.3138/cpj-25-0104 SPECIAL CLINICAL REVIEW FIGURE 1 Number of reported measles cases in Canada, 1998 to 20234 FIGURE 2 Geographic distribution of total measles cases by provinces and territories, 2025 after an infected person has left the area.2,8 Transmission oc- curs through inhalation of infectious droplets, direct contact with respiratory secretions, and activities such as sharing food, drinks, products that produce smoke or vapours, or kissing someone with measles.4,8 Individuals with measles are infec- tious from 4 days before until 4 days after the appearance of the rash.8 The secondary attack rate among susceptible contacts is ≥90%. Incubation and clinical presentation Figure 3 shows the clinical progression of measles.2 It typically begins with prodromal symptoms that start 10 to 14 days (range 7 to 23) post-exposure. Prodromal symptoms include fever, as well as cough, coryza (runny nose), or conjunctivitis. A good way to remember the symptoms is fever plus 3C’s. The prodro- mal phase lasts for 2 to 4 days. Diarrhea can also occur during the prodromal stage.8 Two to 3 days after the prodromal symptoms begin, Koplik spots appear, which occur in 50% to 70% of patients (Figure 4). They are highly characteristic of measles and appear as small, white or gray specks on the buccal mucosa, usually opposite the molars.9 They can also appear on the vaginal or gastrointestinal mucosa or the conjunctival folds. Koplik spots typically appear 1 to 2 days before the rash, and their presence can aid in mak- ing a clinical diagnosis earlier.8,9 As the Koplik spots fade, an erythematous maculopapular rash appears, which spreads in a specific order—beginning at the hairline, spreading to the face, C P J / R P C r J A N U A RY / F E B R U A RY 2 0 2 6 r V O L 1 5 9 , N O 1 33 SPECIAL CLINICAL REVIEW FIGURE 3 Clinical course of primary measles infection Permission obtained from Bird C, Dutton F. How to recognise and manage measles. BMJ 2025; 388: e079895. doi:10.1136/bmj-2024- 079895. FIGURE 4 Koplik spots in a patient with measles Reprinted with permission from Aziz J. Rash inside the mouth [Photo]. Am Fam Physician 2017;95(11):729. then the trunk, arms and, lastly, legs. It lasts 4 to 7 days, fading in the same order of appearance.2,4 Health care professionals should consider measles if a child presents with prodromal symptoms, rash, and diarrhea.2,8 Complications and sequelae Complications occur frequently (in up to 30% of cases) and can appear up to 1 month after infection. Complications are more frequent and severe in pregnant people, children un- der 2 years, and individuals who are immunocompromised.4,8 Notably, measles infection in pregnancy is associated with a higher risk of a low-birth-weight infant, premature labour, and spontaneous abortion. Common complications, occurring in approximately 1 in 10 cases, include otitis media, pneumonia, conjunctivitis, and diarrhea.4,10 Less common but severe complications include respiratory failure and encephalitis, which occur at a rate of 1 in 1000.4,8,10 Encephalitis can occur during the first 7 days of infection, 1 to 6 months after infection, or even years after full recovery.9 Death can occur, but it is rare (rate of 1 to 10 in 10,000 cases of measles) and is mainly due to neurologic or respiratory-related complications.11 Measles infection can lead to a number of long-term sequelae,4,10 including blindness, deafness, and permanent neurological sequelae. The latter category includes subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE), a rare brain disorder char- acterized by behavioural and intellectual deterioration and seizures, which is often fatal. Diagnosis and laboratory testing The Public Health Agency of Canada states that health care providers should “suspect measles in a patient presenting with a febrile illness and rash, or history suggesting that they are not immune to measles, particularly if they have travelled or are known to have had an epidemiologic link to a measles case or outbreak.”12 Other clinical manifestations, such as the prodrome followed by the rash, the progression of the rash and Koplik spots, should raise clinical suspicion for measles. Currently, there is no point-of-care test for measles. To confirm the diagnosis, 2 clinical specimens, either a nasopha- ryngeal or a throat swab, and urine are required for viral detection by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) in addition to serology. This has good sensitivity and specificity for measles detection, particularly within 7 days of rash onset. Measles serology (immunoglobulin M [IgM] and immunoglobulin G [IgG] antibodies) can also be used, but it is not required and may be less reliable in the early stages of the infection. In ad- dition, if the prevalence of measles in the community is low, the positive predictive value of obtaining serology for acute infection (IgM) is decreased significantly. Serological testing may be indicated to determine an individual’s immune status, but testing is not recommended for checking susceptibility be- fore measles vaccination or antibody response after receiving vaccination for measles.13 Infection prevention and control practices Because of the infectiousness of measles, the infection con- trol measures for an active or suspected case include placing a mask on yourself and the patient, isolating the patient with suspected measles into either a private room (if in a commu- nity pharmacy) or a negative-pressure room (in emergency department), and closing the door, ensuring there is a sign on the door. If the pharmacy does not have a private consultation 34 C P J / R P C r J A N U A RY / F E B R U A RY 2 0 2 6 r V O L 1 5 9 , N O 1 SPECIAL CLINICAL REVIEW room, send your patient home wearing a mask. Patients should be instructed to stay at home until their lab results return nega- tive or at least 4 days after rash onset.14 Their exam/clinic room should not be used for 2 hours after the patient has left. If a patient presents with symptoms in the emergency de- partment, notify Infection Prevention and Control, then Public Health, and the Medical Health Officer (MHO). If the patient is in a community pharmacy, call your local health unit and re- port to the MHO. All patient-facing staff must provide evidence of measles immunity, either through 2 MMR vaccinations or a documented positive measles IgG result. Treatment and supportive care Antivirals that target the measles virus are not available. Management is supportive, including adequate hydration and antipyretics to control fever and discomfort. Vitamin A supplementation is recommended for children in resource-limited settings, but it is not routinely used in Canada. Vitamin A deficiency has been linked to delayed recovery and greater complications with measles. Studies conducted in resource-limited countries in the 1980s and 1990s reported that high doses of vitamin A administered orally in 2 daily doses reduced the risk of mortality from measles in children under 2 years of age and shortened the duration of diarrhea and fever by 2 and 1 days, respectively.15 The World Health Organiza- tion (WHO) recommends children diagnosed with measles be given 2 doses of vitamin A supplements. Dosing information can be found in the WHO position paper.16 Given that vitamin A deficiency is uncommon in Canada, routine use of vitamin A in the treatment of measles is not recommended. It may be considered in certain specific situations (such as pre-existing malnutrition) or in severe illness requiring hospitalization. Hospitalization may be required for complications, particu- larly pneumonia or encephalitis. Prevention Vaccination is the key to preventing a measles infection. The recommended age for the first dose is dependent on whether the country has a measles elimination status or not. In coun- tries where measles is endemic, that is, low- to middle-income countries, the first dose is usually given at 9 months of age (can be as early as 6 months).17 In countries with low rates of measles infections, the first dose is given at 12 months of age, as this is the age when maternal antibody levels in the infant will have decreased to a low enough level to optimize the infant’s development of antibodies from the vaccine. The WHO rec- ommends a second dose because 10% to 15% of children who receive only 1 dose do not seroconvert, resulting in a first-dose efficacy of 85% to 90%. With a second dose, efficacy is almost 100%, and lifelong immunity is achieved in most people.8 Dur- ing outbreaks, the WHO recommends an additional dose for children at 6 to 11 months of age. The 2 vaccine products available in Canada are the measles- mumps-rubella (MMR) and combined with varicella (MMRV), which are both live, attenuated vaccines. Note that the MMRV vaccine is authorized for individuals 12 months to less than 13 years of age. The 2 products are considered interchangeable. Routine MMR and MMRV vaccine schedule in Canada18 Children r First dose: 12 to 15 months of age r Second dose: 18 months or 4 to 6 years (depending on province) r Note: If a dose is administered to an infant before 12 months of age due to travel or during an outbreak, it is recom- mended that the infant still receive 2 additional doses, as per the routine immunization schedule. Adults r Two doses of the MMR vaccine are recommended for in- dividuals born on or after January 1, 1970, and for all health care workers born on or after January 1, 1957. Those born earlier are considered immune, as are individuals with a laboratory-confirmed infection or laboratory-confirmed immunity. r Patients with an uncertain immunization history, or those born before 1970 (or before 1957 for health care staff) reporting no history of measles infection, may also be immunized. Measles vaccine before travelling r Early vaccination is strongly recommended for families before travelling to measles-affected areas. r Infants: Children aged 6 to 11 months should be offered an early dose of MMR for protection. This dose will not count towards their series, but it will provide protection against travel-related infections. It will need to be repeated at 12 months of age, as their usual series, which begins at 12 months of age, is started without counting the early dose received. r Young children with 1 dose: Children who are travelling and have received their first dose of measles vaccine at 12 months of age should receive their second dose early, with a minimum interval of 4 weeks after the first dose. r Older children and adults who are travelling and born after January 1, 1970 should be offered an MMR if they are not certain they have had 2 previous doses or have a history of infection. It is important to note that health care workers, travellers, and post-secondary students require some form of documented immunity, either as documented receipt of vaccines, history of laboratory- confirmed infection, or serological confirmation. The vaccine is contraindicated in pregnancy and immunocompromised in- dividuals; susceptible breastfeeding women should receive the MMR vaccine. During a measles outbreak, individuals aged 6 months and older who are susceptible may receive the MMR vaccine. However, if the dose is administered in a child who is 6 months to less than 12 months of age, then 2 additional doses of measles-containing vaccine (given at least 4 weeks apart) must be administered after the child reaches 12 months of age to ensure long-lasting immunity to measles.18 Adverse events and contraindications18 Immunization with a measles-containing vaccine produces mild side effects that occur less frequently than those of a natu- ral infection. They are less frequent with the second dose. Mild reactions include local injection site reactions, such as pain, redness, and swelling, which typically occur 1 to 2 days after vaccination. However, in approximately 5% of children, side effects such as fever, malaise, and a mild rash may develop 1 to 3 weeks after immunization. Parotitis, lymphadenopathy, and joint symptoms can also occur after vaccination. The local reactions of pain, swelling, redness at the injec- tion site, and fever are more common with the MMRV vaccine compared to the MMR vaccine, occurring in 10% of children. In addition to these symptoms, a measles-like, rubella-like, or varicella-like rash can also be seen in 1% to 10% of children afterwards. Serious adverse events and anaphylaxis are infrequent but include immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) that occurs within 6 weeks after immunization, and encephalitis that oc- curs at a rate of 1 per million doses, which is much lower than the rate of natural infection encephalitis, which occurs in 1 per 1000 cases. Febrile seizures following vaccination are observed at a rate of 1 per 2500 doses. This typically occurs when the first MMRV dose is administered to children 12 to 23 months old, whereby the risk of seizure is highest 7 to 10 days post-vaccination. Post-exposure prophylaxis Measles post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) should be consid- ered for individuals at high risk of complications who are not expected to have immunity to measles (i.e., unvaccinated and have never had measles infection). The purpose of PEP is to decrease the likelihood of infection, or if infection does occur, reduce the severity of the disease. Administration of MMR vaccine to non-immune children within 72 hours of exposure to measles has been shown to reduce the risk of developing measles by 83.4% (95% CI 34.4%–95.8%).18 Immunoglobulin administered within 6 days of measles exposure was reported to be 100% effective in preventing measles infection.18 Immunoglobulin is typically administered either intramuscularly or intravenously (depend- ing on the volume of the dose to be administered)…

full_text_sections.full_text: SPECIAL CLINICAL REVIEW PEER-REVIEWED Measles: A resurgent threat and the role of pharmacists in prevention Fawziah Marra BSc(Pharm), PharmD, FCSHP, ACPR, RPh1, Roxane Carr BSc(Pharm), PharmD, FCSHP, ACPR, RPh1,2 Overview Considered eliminated in Canada over 25 years ago, measles has re-emerged as a public health concern due to declining vaccination rates and increased global travel. In fact, recently Canada, and by extension all the Americas, has been stripped of its measles-free certification by the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) after failing to curb an outbreak of the virus for 12 consecutive months.1 The majority of the outbreak cases stem from undervaccinated communities in Alberta and Ontario, although cases have been reported in most provinces and territories. To regain its measles elimination status, vac- cination of the population will play a vital role. As accessible health care providers, pharmacists are in a unique position to detect early signs of disease, educate the public, and play a vital role in vaccination programs. Epidemiology The measles virus is a member of the Paramyxoviridae family, which includes mumps, parainfluenza, and respiratory syncy- tial (RSV) viruses.2 Infection with measles results in lifelong immunity.2 Measles is a nationally notifiable disease.3 The live- attenuated vaccine, containing measles only, was introduced into Canadian routine immunization programs in the early 1970s.4 Between 1974 and 1983, a 1-dose combined vaccine for measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) was introduced. How- ever, Canada moved to the 2-dose MMR vaccine series between 1996 and 1997 with school-based catch-up to ensure chil- 1Faculty of Pharmaceutical Sciences, University of British Columbia, Vancouver, BC; 2BC Children’s Hospital, Vancouver, BC Correspondence: Fawziah Marra, (fawziah@mail.ubc.ca). dren had 2 doses.3,4 Between 1970 and 2024, measles cases decreased by more than 99%.4 The success of the 2-dose MMR campaign allowed Canada to achieve measles elimination status in 1998.3 However, spo- radic outbreaks continued to occur, primarily due to the importation of cases from regions of the world with ongoing transmission or transmission from clusters of unvaccinated individuals. From 1998 to 2023, an average of 91 measles cases were reported annually, ranging between 0 and 752 cases (Figure 1).4 Unfortunately, the number of cases in 2025 has increased exponentially.5 As of November 8, 2025, a total of 5208 measles cases were reported by 10 jurisdictions (Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, New Brunswick, Northwest Territories, Nova Scotia, Ontario, Prince Edward Island, Quebec, and Saskatchewan) (Figure 2).6 Most cases occur in children under 5 and adolescents, particularly those unvaccinated or undervaccinated. Transmission Humans are the only reservoir for measles. The basic repro- duction number (R0) is estimated to be between 12 and 18 (i.e., one infected person will go on to infect 12 to 18 other people). This is approximately 10 times higher than for COVID-19 or influenza,7 making measles one of the most infectious known pathogens. The virus primarily spreads through airborne res- piratory droplets and aerosolized droplet nuclei, which can remain infectious in the air or on surfaces for up to 2 hours © Canadian Pharmacists Association (CPhA), 2026. Please visit https://utppublishing.com/ resources/rights-and-permissions/journals for details. 32 C P J / R P C r J A N U A RY / F E B R U A RY 2 0 2 6 r V O L 1 5 9 , N O 1 DOI:10.3138/cpj-25-0104 SPECIAL CLINICAL REVIEW FIGURE 1 Number of reported measles cases in Canada, 1998 to 20234 FIGURE 2 Geographic distribution of total measles cases by provinces and territories, 2025 after an infected person has left the area.2,8 Transmission oc- curs through inhalation of infectious droplets, direct contact with respiratory secretions, and activities such as sharing food, drinks, products that produce smoke or vapours, or kissing someone with measles.4,8 Individuals with measles are infec- tious from 4 days before until 4 days after the appearance of the rash.8 The secondary attack rate among susceptible contacts is ≥90%. Incubation and clinical presentation Figure 3 shows the clinical progression of measles.2 It typically begins with prodromal symptoms that start 10 to 14 days (range 7 to 23) post-exposure. Prodromal symptoms include fever, as well as cough, coryza (runny nose), or conjunctivitis. A good way to remember the symptoms is fever plus 3C’s. The prodro- mal phase lasts for 2 to 4 days. Diarrhea can also occur during the prodromal stage.8 Two to 3 days after the prodromal symptoms begin, Koplik spots appear, which occur in 50% to 70% of patients (Figure 4). They are highly characteristic of measles and appear as small, white or gray specks on the buccal mucosa, usually opposite the molars.9 They can also appear on the vaginal or gastrointestinal mucosa or the conjunctival folds. Koplik spots typically appear 1 to 2 days before the rash, and their presence can aid in mak- ing a clinical diagnosis earlier.8,9 As the Koplik spots fade, an erythematous maculopapular rash appears, which spreads in a specific order—beginning at the hairline, spreading to the face, C P J / R P C r J A N U A RY / F E B R U A RY 2 0 2 6 r V O L 1 5 9 , N O 1 33 SPECIAL CLINICAL REVIEW FIGURE 3 Clinical course of primary measles infection Permission obtained from Bird C, Dutton F. Rash inside the mouth [Photo]. Am Fam Physician 2017;95(11):729. then the trunk, arms and, lastly, legs. It lasts 4 to 7 days, fading in the same order of appearance.2,4 Health care professionals should consider measles if a child presents with prodromal symptoms, rash, and diarrhea.2,8 Complications and sequelae Complications occur frequently (in up to 30% of cases) and can appear up to 1 month after infection. Complications are more frequent and severe in pregnant people, children un- der 2 years, and individuals who are immunocompromised.4,8 Notably, measles infection in pregnancy is associated with a higher risk of a low-birth-weight infant, premature labour, and spontaneous abortion. Common complications, occurring in approximately 1 in 10 cases, include otitis media, pneumonia, conjunctivitis, and diarrhea.4,10 Less common but severe complications include respiratory failure and encephalitis, which occur at a rate of 1 in 1000.4,8,10 Encephalitis can occur during the first 7 days of infection, 1 to 6 months after infection, or even years after full recovery.9 Death can occur, but it is rare (rate of 1 to 10 in 10,000 cases of measles) and is mainly due to neurologic or respiratory-related complications.11 Measles infection can lead to a number of long-term sequelae,4,10 including blindness, deafness, and permanent neurological sequelae. The latter category includes subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE), a rare brain disorder char- acterized by behavioural and intellectual deterioration and seizures, which is often fatal. analysis.research_question_and_background: Studies conducted in resource-limited countries in the 1980s and 1990s reported that high doses of vitamin A administered orally in 2 daily doses reduced the risk of mortality from measles in children under 2 years of age and shortened the duration of diarrhea and fever by 2 and 1 days, respectively.15 The World Health Organiza- tion (WHO) recommends children diagnosed with measles be given 2 doses of vitamin A supplements.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Common complications, occurring in approximately 1 in 10 cases, include otitis media, pneumonia, conjunctivitis, and diarrhea.4,10 Less common but severe complications include respiratory failure and encephalitis, which occur at a rate of 1 in 1000.4,8,10 Encephalitis can occur during the first 7 days of infection, 1 to 6 months after infection, or even years after full recovery.9 Death can occur, but it is rare (rate of 1 to 10 in 10,000 cases of measles) and is mainly due to neurologic or respiratory-related complications.11 Measles infection can lead to a number of long-term sequelae,4,10 including blindness, deafness, and permanent neurological sequelae.
analysis.methods: To confirm the diagnosis, 2 clinical specimens, either a nasopha- ryngeal or a throat swab, and urine are required for viral detection by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) in addition to serology.
analysis.main_results: In coun- tries where measles is endemic, that is, low- to middle-income countries, the first dose is usually given at 9 months of age (can be as early as 6 months).17 In countries with low rates of measles infections, the first dose is given at 12 months of age, as this is the age when maternal antibody levels in the infant will have decreased to a low enough level to optimize the infant’s development of antibodies from the vaccine.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The local reactions of pain, swelling, redness at the injec- tion site, and fever are more common with the MMRV vaccine compared to the MMR vaccine, occurring in 10% of children.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Prevention Vaccination is the key to preventing a measles infection.
